prompt: Each pencil costs \$$0.25$. How many can you buy with \$$3.00$?
hint: You know the total money and the price of one item. Which operation tells you how many equal prices fit into the total?

hints.title: 🔁 Another angle
hints.text: A pencil costs one quarter of a dollar. Think about how many quarters make a single dollar, then how many make three.
You know the total money and the price of one item. Which operation tells you how many equal prices fit into the total?
Set up $3.00 \div 0.25$. Multiplying both numbers by $100$ turns it into $300 \div 25$, which is easier to work out.

explanation: To find how many pencils the money buys, divide the total by the price of one pencil: $3.00 \div 0.25$.
Multiply both numbers by $100$ to remove the decimals. The quotient stays the same, and the problem becomes $300 \div 25$.
Four $25$s make $100$, so there are $4 \times 3 = 12$ of them in $300$.
You can buy $12$ pencils with $3$ dollars.
